summary: Rurutu Airport (RUR) is a regional airport serving Rurutu Island, part of the remote Austral Islands archipelago in French Polynesia. Located in the southernmost reaches of French Polynesia, the airport provides essential air connectivity to one of the lesser-visited island groups in the territory. The facility features a single runway and primarily handles inter-island domestic flights operated by Air Tahiti.
faqs:
Q: Which airlines operate from Rurutu Airport?
A: Air Tahiti is the primary airline serving Rurutu, operating propeller aircraft on routes connecting the island to Tahiti (Papeete) and other Austral Islands.

Q: How far is the airport from the main village of Moerai?
A: The airport is located on the northern side of the island, approximately 10-15 minutes by road from Moerai, the main village.

Q: When is the best time to visit Rurutu?
A: The dry season from May to October is generally considered ideal, with cooler temperatures. The humpback whale watching season runs roughly from July to October.

Q: Are there customs and immigration facilities at Rurutu Airport?
A: As a domestic airport within French Polynesia, Rurutu handles internal flights and does not process international arrivals, which are handled at Faa'a International Airport in Tahiti.
transport_tips: Rental cars and scooters are available at or near the airport and are recommended given the limited public transport on the island. Taxi services are available but should be arranged in advance, especially for early morning or late evening flights. The road network connects all villages on the island and provides access to key attractions including limestone caves and whale watching lookouts.
local_tip: Bring a light jacket even in summer — Rurutu is one of the southernmost inhabited islands of French Polynesia and can be surprisingly cool and windy, especially during whale watching season when temperatures drop noticeably.
